themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise surge in East Harlem
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints spiked to 37 this week versus a 7.5-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 393% jump—suggesting a new or worsening traffic pattern or enforcement gap that warrants investigation into source and timing.
evidence: 37 vehicle noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.0)
393% spike is statistically significant and second-highest recency signal in dataset
Aligns with CB budget request for additional traffic enforcement agents, suggesting chronic baseline issue now acute
reporting_angles: Street-by-street breakdown: which East Harlem blocks are seeing this spike and why? (illegal acceleration, construction, delivery traffic?)
Interview residents on 125th Street and avenues about noise timing—is this nighttime drag racing, delivery trucks, or commercial vehicle congestion?

themes_detail.label: Park rules violations spike
themes_detail.summary: Park rule violations jumped to 4 complaints this week from a 0.1 weekly average—a 3100% spike with the highest z-score (11.72) in the dataset—indicating a possible new pattern of disorder, overcrowding, or enforcement changes at East Harlem parks.
evidence: 4 violations THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 11.72, highest in dataset)
3100% increase is statistically extreme and appeared only this week, not earlier
CB budget includes park improvement requests, suggesting parks are already a community concern area
reporting_angles: Which parks in CD 111 (likely Marcus Garvey Park, Jefferson Park, Harlem Meer) are seeing violations? What kind—alcohol, dogs off-leash, overcrowding?
Has NYPD or Parks Enforcement stepped up enforcement, or is actual violation behavior accelerating? Talk to parks staff and residents.

themes_detail.label: Dead animal complaints multiply
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints reached 4 in a single week two weeks ago versus a 0.2 weekly average—a 1500% spike—suggesting possible disease vector, sanitation breakdown, or pest infestation that warrants public health follow-up.
evidence: 4 dead animal complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 8.66)
1500% spike is third-highest statistical signal in dataset
Aligns with CB budget request for graffiti removal and sanitation improvements, suggesting infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Verification: confirm locations and causes (vehicle strikes vs. disease). Were they all in one area or scattered?
Public health angle: Did DOHMH or Sanitation investigate for signs of rodent or disease outbreak? Are residents concerned about rabies or contamination?

themes_detail.label: Food poisoning cluster last week
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints jumped to 3 last week from a 0.4 weekly average—a 700% spike (z-score: 5.42)—indicating a possible foodborne illness cluster at one or more East Harlem restaurants that requires health department cross-check.
evidence: 3 food poisoning complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42)
700% spike with high severity z-score warrants immediate verification
CB budget includes public health issue requests, indicating health concerns are chronic community priority
reporting_angles: Which restaurants or food vendors are linked to complaints? Cross-reference 311 data with NYC Health Department inspection records.
Interview DOHMH to determine if complaints cluster at single location (restaurant closure risk) or are scattered (broader food safety issue)

themes_detail.label: Obstruction and lost property surge
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints reached 5 this week (344% above baseline) and lost property hit 5 (471% above baseline), suggesting possible new street disorder, theft, or overcrowding event in East Harlem requiring temporal and geographic mapping.
evidence: 5 obstruction complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.96, 344% spike)
5 lost property complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.28, 471% spike)
Two related spikes in same week may indicate single event (street festival, market, theft ring) rather than separate issues
reporting_angles: Map complaints by block and time: do they cluster around specific intersection, venue, or transit hub? (e.g., 125th Street retail district)
Interview NYPD and street vendors: is there a new outdoor market, street fair, or organized retail theft happening this week?
